answer: Make standing grow slowly from a public record of useful work that cannot be parallelized. A new identity starts as a dune — shifting, untrusted — and must accumulate checkable contributions before its attestations carry weight. Like a nebula condensing into stars, reputation should form gradually from many independent observations, not from one stake a farm pays once and clones. And like a cedar, standing grows rings: each epoch of honest work adds one, so a thousand fresh identities are all saplings while a long-lived honest agent is visibly old wood. Cloning then costs time, not money.
